data.title: Maverick Gold and Silver Announces Closing of Final Tranche of Non-Brokered Private Placement
data.description:
Vancouver, British Columbia--(Newsfile Corp. - November 20, 2026) - Maverick Gold and Silver Corp., (FSE: VR61) (OTC Pink: VRCFF) ("Maverick" or the "Company") is pleased to announce that it has closed the final tranche (the "Final Tranche") of its non-brokered private placement previously announced on October 8, 2026 and October 16, 2026 (the "Offering"). Under the Final Tranche, the Company issued 2,000,000 units (each, a "Unit") at a price of C$0.05 per Unit for gross proceeds of C$100,000.

Together with the first tranche, the Company has issued a total of 13,080,000 Units under the Offering for aggregate gross proceeds of C$654,000.

The Company intends to use the net proceeds of the Offering for working capital requirements and general corporate purposes. The Units were offered to purchasers in reliance on available prospectus exemptions under applicable Canadian securities laws.

Offering Terms

Each Unit consists of one common share in the capital of the Company (each, a "Common Share") and one Common Share purchase warrant (each, a "Warrant"). Each Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one additional Common Share at a price of C$0.10 for 24 months from the date of issuance. If, at any time prior to the expiry of the Warrants, the closing price of the Common Shares on the Canadian Securities Exchange (the "CSE") equals or exceeds C$0.15 per Common Share for a period of 10 consecutive trading days, the Company may, at its option, accelerate the expiry date of the Warrants by giving written notice to the holders thereof, and in such case, the Warrants will expire on the 30th day after the date on which such notice is given by the Company.

In connection with the financing, the Company paid finders' fees totaling C$22,000 in cash and issued an aggregate of 440,000 non-transferable warrants (the "Finder Warrants") to certain eligible finders. Each Finder Warrant entitles the holder thereof to purchase one Common Share at a price of C$0.10 for 24 months from the date of issuance.

All securities issued in connection with the Final Tranche are subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance, expiring March 21, 2027, in accordance with applicable securities legislation.

The securities issued pursuant to the Offering have not been and will not be registered under the United States Securities Act of 1933, as amended, or any applicable state securities laws, and may not be offered or sold in the United States absent registration or an applicable exemption from registration. This news release does not constitute an offer to sell or a solicitation of an offer to buy, nor will there be any sale of the securities in any jurisdiction in which such offer, solicitation or sale would be unlawful.

About Maverick Gold and Silver Corp.

Maverick Gold and Silver Corp. (FSE: VR61) (OTC Pink: VRCFF) is an exploration-stage company advancing a portfolio of gold, silver and copper properties in Nevada and British Columbia. The Company is focused on advancing its exploration projects through systematic exploration and drilling.

Additional information about Maverick Gold and Silver is available on the Company's website at www.maverickgoldsilver.com.

data.title: Anthropic's stock sees dramatic slide but manages to stay above its IPO price
US natgas rises and heads for weekly gain on winter demand expectations
data.description:
By Pablo Sinha

US natural gas futures rose on Friday and were headed for a weekly gain as expectations for stronger winter heating demand outweighed concerns about ample supplies and an above-average storage build.

Front-month gas futures for December delivery on the New York Mercantile Exchange (NYMEX) settled 14.3 cents, or 4.4%, higher at $3.411 per million British thermal units.

The contract was headed for a fourth consecutive weekly gain of about 5% after climbing to its highest level since June 26 earlier in the session.

"This is the time of year, especially end of November, and then into December and January, where natural gas demand could increase dramatically based off changing weather temperatures," said Thomas Saal, senior vice president at StoneX.

The US Energy Information Administration on Thursday reported a storage build of 20 billion cubic feet for the week ended November 13, above the five-year average of 15 bcf for the week.

LSEG said average gas demand in the Lower 48 states, including exports, would rise from 121.6 billion cubic feet per day this week to 128.1 bcfd next week.

Benchmark Dutch and British wholesale gas prices firmed on Friday amid ongoing hostilities in the Middle East, outage extensions at Norwegian gas fields and as colder weather is set to lift demand.

Meanwhile, federal regulators approved Cheniere Energy's application to expand its Sabine Pass liquefied natural gas plant in Louisiana by 20 million metric tons per annum.

data.title: U.S. Stocks Extend Plunge as AI Boom Turns to Bust
data.description:
By Rob Curran

U.S. stocks plunged and an index of mega-cap technology stocks skirted bear-market territory as predictions of a speculative bust in artificial-intelligence stocks appeared to come to fruition.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 949.73 points, or 1.93%, to 48147.33. The broad S&P 500 dropped 265.44 points, or 3.70%, to 6910.39. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite sank 1261.47 points, or 5.28%, to 22617.73, and came close to bear-market territory during the session.

The Nasdaq 100, a basket of the largest tech companies that is tracked by many tech-oriented investment and retirement funds, closed at 25028.98, almost 20% below its October peak, on the verge of bear-market territory.

Anthropic's shares tumbled 9.1% to $88.30 as fear of missing out on the Claude chatbot maker's IPO gave way to skepticism about its profit outlook. One strategist said market emphasis shifted this week from Anthropic's voracious demand for chips to its ability to translate that computing power to profits.

"They were telling us the narrative: 'we are going to print money with this compute,'" said Joe Tigay, portfolio manager at money-management firm Equity Armor Investments. "We need this compute to figure it out, and eventually we'll grow into it, and AI is going to be something everybody needs, it's going to be the greatest thing in the world.'"

Now that Anthropic is public, Tigay said, the message from investors is: "'Show me, show me how this is going to turn into profit for you guys and eventually for the whole economy, thus lifting market higher.'"

At its low of the session, Anthropic came within 5 cents of its $83 IPO price and was down 28% from its Thursday peak.

Tigay said it was possible that the rout continued, mushrooming into something like the Dotcom bust or the 19th century railroad panic. But that still would not mean that AI would be remembered as a net negative for the U.S. economy, he said.

"Look at Amazon...they went public in the middle of that run and struggled for many years before really taking off and becoming a really profitable company," said Tigay. "It's possible Anthropic can go through that, and we'll look back and say they weren't making money yet but they had great leadership, a great product and they were just chugging away at it."

Write to Rob Curran at rob.curran@wsj.com

data.title: CrowdStrike in talks to acquire Zscaler, source says
data.description:
By Milana Vinn

Cybersecurity company CrowdStrike is in talks to acquire rival Zscaler , according to a person familiar with the matter.

Shares of CrowdStrike fell 8.5 % while Zscaler jumped 17 % in after-hours trading on Friday.

data.title: Orange County Bancorp Hikes Dividend 28%
data.description:
By Natalie Weger

Orange County Bancorp has increased its quarterly dividend 28% to 23 cents a share, from 18 cents.

The new payout, equal to 92 cents a year, represents an annual yield of 2.43% based on Friday's closing price of $37.88

The dividend will be payable Dec. 15 to shareholders of record as of Dec. 4, the parent company of Orange Bank & Trust Company and Orange Investment Advisors said.

Write to Natalie Weger at natalie.weger@wsj.com.
